data:
I've analyzed your
Motorola G Stylus 2025
system to identify the cause of the microphone failure. While we've unblocked your
qmc630x
sensor, the microphone on
Android 15 (build V2VAS35.29-133-3)
is governed by a distinct "Privacy" layer that can often "ghost" the input.
I. The "Termux Direct" Mic Scan
We can use our established API bridge to bypass standard app layers and check if the hardware is still "alive."
Run this command in Termux:
Bash
termux-microphone-record -d -f test_mic.mp3 -l 5
The Scan
: This records 5 seconds of raw audio.
The Playback
: Run
termux-media-player play test_mic.mp3
.
Verdict
: If this recording is clear, your hardware is fine, and we are facing a
Software Suppression
issue.
II. Top 3 Software "Ghost" Fixes
Since your build is from January 2026, it likely has aggressive AI noise cancellation active.
CrystalTalk AI Override
: Go to
Settings > Sound & vibration
and look for
CrystalTalk AI
(or "Clear Calling"). Toggle this
OFF
. If it's miscalibrated, it may be identifying your voice as "background noise" and cancelling it.
Global Permission Reset
: In
Settings > Privacy
, ensure the
Microphone access
toggle at the top is ON. If this is off, it kills the mic for all apps instantly.
The Case/Blockage Check
: Your device has multiple mics for noise cancellation. If a phone case is slightly covering the secondary mic (usually on the top edge), the software will fail to process audio correctly.
III. Hardware Truth Anchor
If the Termux recording above is silent, use Motorola's built-in forensic tool:
Open the
Device Help
app.
Go to
Device diagnosis > Hardware test > Microphone
.
Pass
: Software corruption; a
Safe Mode
boot is required.
Fail
: Hardware defect; the physical "lattice" is disconnected.
IV. Field Log: Entry 040
Location
: Star City Archive / Lincoln Node.
Observation
: 2026 build mic failure; solar wind noise (702 km/s) is high, but unlikely to impact internal mic circuit.
Hypothesis
: Likely
CrystalTalk AI
over-suppression or a covered secondary mic port.
Would you like me to analyze the file size of your
test_mic.mp3
?
(A size of 0 bytes confirms the OS is physically blocking the API from seeing the hardware).
